mo_harmony_creek_boulders.blurb: A compact cluster of boulders in Astral Valley, east Missouri, holding around 25 problems and one of the denser concentrations of rock in the valley. Everything here is bouldering. The spread is wide: a couple of very easy warm-ups, a solid middle of V2 to V5 problems, and a handful of harder lines reaching V7. Expect plenty of overhanging rock, with a mix of powerful and technical movement, so it suits climbers who like steep, burly sequences. The landing zones sit right beside a fire pit area, which makes it easy to bring a group and rotate on problems. Bring enough pads, since the ground is uneven.

mo_cm_jacktar_hollow.blurb: A wooded boulder field in the Paddy Creek Wilderness of the Mark Twain National Forest, in south-central Missouri. Roughly two dozen problems are recorded, all bouldering, with most falling between V2 and V5 and a few stiffer ones up to V7 and a single standout near the top of the scale. It is a quiet, undeveloped feel rather than a polished park: you hike into the trees, follow a shallow drainage, and the boulders start along its left side. The trail can be easy to miss, so carry a map. It is a good pick for climbers who want solitude and a mid-grade tick list.

mo_providence_main_wall.blurb: The steepest and hardest section of the Providence bluffs, on the Missouri River side of Columbia. About 25 routes, mostly bolted sport lines with some trad, plus a layback and a crack. The grade spread leans hard: a few old easy routes at the bottom end, a few in the 5.8 to 5.10 range, then a strong core of 5.11 and 5.12 that makes this one of the state's better places for that level. Many lines have seen few ascents, so grades may shift as holds clean up. Expect a short bluff beside the bike trail, with trees screening the noise.
mo_providence_main_wall.parking_note: From Columbia, head about five miles south along Providence Road until you see the signs for the river landing, then follow them to the lot.
mo_providence_main_wall.approach: Walk east along the Katy Trail for a bit under half a mile, then scramble up a steep path to the base of the bluffs.

mo_south_area.blurb: The friendlier end of the Providence bluffs near Columbia, Missouri, with about two dozen routes, nearly all bolted sport lines and a few trad or mixed ones. Grades stretch from the high 5.7s through the 5.12s, but the heart of the wall is 5.9 and 5.10, with a smaller share of 5.11 and 5.12. The cliff has slabby sections, a long roof, some cracks and a drainage gully. Quality is uneven, though easier lines do exist, which makes it a reasonable stop for newer leaders. In summer the face is shaded, and mornings are the best time to climb.
mo_south_area.parking_note: From Columbia, head about five miles south along Providence Road until you see the signs for the river landing, then follow them to the lot.
mo_south_area.approach: From the lot, follow the Katy Trail east for under half a mile, then take the steep path up to the base of the cliff.

mo_h_prison_wall.blurb: A sport wall on the north side of Robinson Bluff, in eastern Missouri, with 24 bolted routes whose names riff on famous jails and, at the far end, prison-themed songs. Nearly all of the grades sit in 5.10 and 5.11, with a dozen or so in the 5.10 range, a few easier warm-ups in the 5.7 to 5.9 band, and one route at 5.12. The harder lines mostly cluster toward the climber's-right end of the wall. A good spot for a day of steady, mid-grade sport climbing.
mo_h_prison_wall.approach: From the lot, go to the staircase on the bluff and head north along the base, climber's right. The path passes beneath the Van Gogh Wall, then drops down and around to Prison Wall.

mo_rooftown.blurb: The first bouldering zone you reach along the Turkey Creek Trail in the Three Creeks area, between Columbia and Ashland, Missouri. Two large roofs anchor the zone, with several other boulders around them, and 24 problems are recorded. The range is unusually broad: several easy problems from V0 to V2, a good number at V4 and V5, and then a few serious projects reaching into the double digits. The boulders sit close to the creek bed, which is normally dry but can flood after heavy rain and stay wet for a week or more, so check recent weather before you go.

mo_upper_trail_area.blurb: Sandstone boulders in the Paddy Creek Wilderness of the Mark Twain National Forest, in south-central Missouri. These are the first blocs you meet on the upper hiking trail, just before the slide. About two dozen problems are recorded, all bouldering, starting at V2 and rising to V9, with the bulk between V3 and V7. The terrain is wilderness woods with a backcountry feel, so expect short walks, uneven ground and little in the way of signage. It suits strong boulderers who enjoy arete and crimp style problems and want a quiet day among the trees.
mo_upper_trail_area.approach: Use the upper trailhead, across from the campground, and follow the upper trail to the first boulders just before the slide.

mo_colony_wall.blurb: The main sport wall at Rockwoods Reservation, in Wildwood on the west side of the St. Louis area. About 22 bolted routes, with a friendly spread: a handful at 5.7, a few at 5.8 and 5.9, a solid block of 5.10s, and a few 5.11s and one 5.12. It is a short, nature-filled outing, set on a former quarry face, with birds and other wildlife around, and it is close enough to town for an after-work session. A strong choice for newer leaders and anyone building mileage.
mo_colony_wall.parking_note: The trailhead is on Christy Road, just off Highway 109, roughly half a mile north of the reservation's main entrance.
mo_colony_wall.approach: A quarter-mile natural-surface trail climbs the hill from the lot. Turn left at the signs and the wall begins from there.

_conflicts.mo_cm_jacktar_hollow: Stored rock is dolomite, but the Paddy Creek Wilderness page calls the area's rock sandstone (https://mountainproject.com/area/113901772/cm-paddy-creek-wilderness).
_conflicts.mo_providence_main_wall: Stored rock is dolomite, but the Providence page describes limestone with chert bands (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/112174683/cm-providence).
_conflicts.mo_south_area: Stored rock is dolomite, but the Providence page describes limestone with chert bands (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/112174683/cm-providence).
